What is AI engineering?.expected_definition: The technical field of designing, building, evaluating, and operating useful applications and systems using pretrained foundation models (mainly LLMs) as components. It focuses on selecting models, connecting them to data and tools, and iterating on evaluation and improvement, rather than building models from scratch.

What is LoRA?.expected_definition: A PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights, represents weight updates as a low-rank product of two small matrices, and trains only those small matrices. It trains few parameters and saves the results (adapters) in small files. The Lecture 02 exercises cover LoRA.

What is QLoRA?.expected_definition: A method that saves memory by quantizing base-model weights to, for example, 4 bits, then trains with LoRA. This lets smaller GPUs handle larger models. In the Lecture 02 exercises, the model fits in GPU memory, so we train with LoRA and compare memory and output differences when loading in 4-bit in the advanced section.

What is Quantization?.expected_definition: A technique for representing model weights with fewer bits (for example, from 16 bits to 4 bits) to reduce memory use and computation. Accuracy may decrease slightly.

What is Hallucination?.expected_definition: The phenomenon of an LLM generating plausible content that is factually incorrect or nonexistent. It is more likely when asked about things the model does not know, such as recent information or organization- or course-specific details. Mitigations include consulting external data through tools, asking for evidence, and detecting errors through evaluation.

What is Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)?.expected_definition: A method of further training a model using pairs of inputs and desired outputs, such as questions and reference answers. A representative method for teaching instruction-following behavior.

What is PEFT?.expected_definition: An umbrella term for methods that train only a small subset of model parameters or a small set of added parameters instead of all parameters. This can greatly reduce GPU memory and storage requirements. LoRA is a representative example.

What are the 3 homework levels?.expected_definition: The structure of AIE2026 homework. There are three levels: "Basic (review lecture content)", "Implementation (write your own code)", and "Advanced (research and experimentation)". Completing any one level completes the homework for that lecture. As a rule, it is not graded.

What is a lecNN-start tag?.expected_definition: A Git tag on the starting code for each lecture's exercises in the AIE2026 course repository (for example, lec03-start). Even if you have not finished the previous lecture, creating a branch from this tag lets you start the current lecture's exercises.

What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?.expected_definition: An open standard protocol connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources. Tools exposed through an MCP server can be used in a common way from compatible agents and editors (MCP clients). In Lecture 05, you will experience this by turning glossary search into an MCP server.

Where should I store my API key so it is.expected_definition: A secret value registered in your GitHub account settings. It is passed as an environment variable when you start Codespaces for a selected repository. When registering it, select the repository you will use (your own fork). If registered while a Codespace is running, restart the Codespace.

What happens when a fine-tuned model mem.expected_definition: A state in which the model fits training data excessively and performs worse on unseen inputs. Detect it by measuring performance on validation data not used for training.

Which sampling parameter controls random.expected_definition: A setting that adjusts randomness when choosing the next token. Lower values make outputs more stable; higher values make them more varied. This is one reason the same question can yield different answers.

What do we call an LLM system that combi.expected_definition: A system that achieves a goal through a loop in which an LLM decides to call tools, examines the results, and decides its next action. Its basic structure is "model + loop + tools".

How do we propose merging changes from a.expected_definition: A mechanism for requesting that changes from one branch be merged into another. It supports reviewing differences, comments, and displaying automated test results. Submit work for this course as a PR from your working branch to main within your own fork.

What constraint or check prevents undesi.expected_definition: A constraint or check designed to prevent undesirable agent behavior or outputs. Methods include rules in instructions, restricting tool permissions, checking outputs, and requesting human confirmation before important operations.

How do the automated pytest tests verify.expected_definition: A fake model included in Pydantic AI for testing. It calls tools and returns dummy answers without calling a real LLM. It lets you test agent wiring (whether tools are registered, called, and return results) without an API key or usage allowance.
